name: Naturalisation (Irish Citizenship)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 5 years of 'reckonable residence' within the last 9 years, including 1 continuous year immediately before applying. Must hold Stamp 4 or 5 at time of application. Student and asylum-seeker time is NOT reckonable.
This requires good character — assessed with ministerial discretion, not an automatic entitlement even when residence criteria are technically met.

requirement_groups.name: Spouse/civil partner of an Irish citizen

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 3 years of marriage/civil partnership and 3 of the last 5 years of residence.

evidence_required.document: Declaration of fidelity and attendance at a citizenship ceremony

notes: GENUINE, CONFIRMED PROCESSING-TIME IMPROVEMENT worth flagging prominently — a rare positive counter-trend in this dataset, which more often documents backlogs worsening: per a Ministerial Oireachtas written answer (24 March 2026, ref 22096/26), the median processing time for a naturalisation decision was approximately 8 months in 2024-2025, down from 15 months (2023), 19 months (2022), and 24 months (2021) — a genuine, dated, multi-year improvement credited to the new online process introduced October 2023. Note this is time-to-DECISION specifically; the full path to certificate/ceremony can still run 12-20 months, a real distinction worth surfacing. Fees confirmed: €175 application (non-refundable) + €950 certification on approval (€200 for minors/widow(er)s; free for refugees). Dual citizenship confirmed permitted. PROPOSAL NOT YET LAW, flagged consistently with how this dataset handles similar cases: a DHS-equivalent proposed fee increase (€175→higher, €950 certification also proposed to rise) was NOT confirmed as enacted during this research pass — encoded fees reflect current, operative figures only.
